clauses: Use the average institutional ownership across all non-missing ownership records as the benchmark.
Use the mean of the timing groups’ average ownership, including the missing-timing group, as the benchmark.
readings: Looking at announcement timing (`eventannotm`, with a missing timing as its own group), which timings have an average institutional ownership strictly above average? Ignoring missing ownership values, give in one row the mean of those timings' average ownership and how far above average they are on average, without rounding. Use the average institutional ownership across all non-missing ownership records as the benchmark.

Looking at announcement timing (`eventannotm`, with a missing timing as its own group), which timings have an average institutional ownership strictly above average? Ignoring missing ownership values, give in one row the mean of those timings' average ownership and how far above average they are on average, without rounding. Use the mean of the timing groups’ average ownership, including the missing-timing group, as the benchmark.
queries:
WITH benchmark AS (
    SELECT AVG(instownpct) AS overall_avg
    FROM sentimentandfundamentals
),
timing_averages AS (
    SELECT eventannotm, AVG(instownpct) AS timing_avg
    FROM sentimentandfundamentals
    GROUP BY eventannotm
)
SELECT
    AVG(timing_avg) AS mean_ownership,
    AVG(timing_avg - overall_avg) AS mean_above_average
FROM timing_averages
CROSS JOIN benchmark
WHERE timing_avg > overall_avg

WITH timing_averages AS (
  SELECT eventannotm, AVG(instownpct) AS avg_ownership
  FROM sentimentandfundamentals
  GROUP BY eventannotm
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ownership) AS avg_ownership
  FROM timing_averages
)
SELECT
  AVG(t.avg_ownership) AS mean_ownership,
  AVG(t.avg_ownership - b.avg_ownership) AS mean_above_average
FROM timing_averages AS t
CROSS JOIN benchmark AS b
WHERE t.avg_ownership > b.avg_ownership
